# Implementation Plan: Lead Management with AI Qualification

**Branch**: `001-lead-crud-ai` | **Date**: 2025-12-31 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-lead-crud-ai/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/sp.plan` command. See `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

Implement REST API for lead CRUD operations with AI-powered BANT qualification using **Kubernetes microservices architecture**. The system enables sales teams to create, view, update, and delete leads while automatically scoring prospects using Anthropic Claude API across four dimensions: Budget (0-25), Authority (0-25), Need (0-25), and Timeline (0-25). The implementation follows **event-driven patterns with Redpanda (Kafka) messaging**, **Dapr distributed application runtime**, Redis state management, and comprehensive observability through Prometheus/Grafana.

**Architecture Shift**: This plan deviates from Constitution Principle I (Serverless-First) in favor of Kubernetes for cost savings (~40% reduction), vendor portability, and team expertise alignment. See [ADR 0001](../../history/adr/0001-kubernetes-over-serverless.md) for full justification.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.3+ with Node.js 20 (Docker containers)
**Primary Dependencies**: Express.js 4.x, Dapr SDK (@dapr/dapr), Anthropic SDK, pg (PostgreSQL client), KafkaJS (Redpanda client)
**Storage**: Neon DB PostgreSQL 15 (serverless), Redis 7 (Dapr state store), Redpanda Cloud (event streaming)
**Testing**: Jest (unit tests), Supertest (integration tests), Testcontainers (integration with real services)
**Target Platform**: DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS) with Minikube for local development
**Project Type**: Web application (backend API + future frontend, containerized microservices)
**Performance Goals**:
- Lead CRUD operations: <200ms p95 latency
- AI qualification: <3000ms p95 latency
- Lead list queries: <500ms p95 for 10K leads
- Support 100 concurrent requests
- Cache hit rate >70%

**Constraints**:
- Kubernetes-based (containerized deployments)
- GDPR compliant (24hr deletion processing)
- Rate limiting: 100 req/hour for lead creation
- Budget: $161/month for DOKS (3-node cluster) + $0-99/month Redpanda (free tier available)
- RTO: 1 hour, RPO: 5 minutes

**Scale/Scope**:
- 10,000 active leads
- 6 API endpoints (POST, GET list, GET by ID, PATCH, DELETE, POST qualify)
- 4 database tables (leads, lead_scores, users, activity_logs)
- 4 Kafka topics (lead-events, notifications, follow-up-events, ai-qualification)
- 3 microservices (backend-api, notification-service, follow-up-service)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Pre-Phase 0 Validation

| Principle | Compliance | Evidence |
|-----------|------------|----------|
| I. Serverless-First Architecture | ⚠️ **DEVIATION** | **Using Kubernetes instead of AWS Lambda.** Justified by ADR 0001: 40% cost savings ($161/month vs $350/month), vendor portability, team expertise. State still in managed services (Neon DB, Redis). |
| II. Event-Driven Communication | ✅ PASS | Redpanda (Kafka) + Dapr Pub/Sub for lead lifecycle events, async processing with consumer groups |
| III. AI-Driven Qualification (BANT) | ✅ PASS | Claude API with structured 4-category scoring (25 points each), same as original |
| IV. Security by Design | ✅ PASS | JWT auth (via Dapr middleware), TLS encryption, RBAC, rate limiting, parameterized queries |
| V. Observability and Monitoring | ✅ PASS | Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, structured JSON logging, Dapr tracing |
| VI. Test-First Development | ⚠️ PARTIAL | Plan includes test strategy; implementation will follow TDD with 80% coverage target |
| VII. Performance and Scalability | ✅ PASS | SLAs defined: <200ms CRUD, <3000ms AI, <500ms list queries; Horizontal Pod Autoscaling |
| VIII. Cost Optimization | ✅ **IMPROVED** | **$161/month DOKS (40% cheaper than AWS $350/month)**, Redpanda free tier, 90-day archival |
| IX. Compliance and Data Governance | ✅ PASS | GDPR deletion within 24hr, 7-year audit logs, 2-year retention, 90-day archival |
| X. Disaster Recovery | ✅ PASS | Neon DB backups, Kubernetes manifests in Git (IaC), Helm chart versioning |

**Overall**: PASS with justified deviation - Principle I deviation documented in [ADR 0001](../../history/adr/0001-kubernetes-over-serverless.md). Cost optimization actually **improved** (40% savings). All other principles satisfied.

**Structure Decision**: Selected **Kubernetes microservices architecture** with:
- **Backend API**: Express.js REST API with Dapr sidecar
- **Notification Service**: Dapr Pub/Sub subscriber for email/WhatsApp notifications
- **Follow-up Service**: Dapr Cron Binding for recurring tasks
- **Helm Charts**: Parameterized deployment for multi-environment (dev, prod)
- **Dapr Components**: Infrastructure abstraction (Kafka, Redis, Secrets)
- **Docker Compose**: Local development with Redpanda + Redis
- **GitHub Actions**: CI/CD pipeline for DOKS deployment

## Complexity Tracking

> **Fill ONLY if Constitution Check has violations that must be justified**

| Violation | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|-----------|------------|-------------------------------------|
| Kubernetes instead of AWS Lambda (Principle I) | **Cost**: $161/month vs $350/month (40% savings)<br/>**Portability**: Avoid AWS vendor lock-in<br/>**Team Skills**: Existing Kubernetes expertise | **AWS Serverless**: Higher cost ($350-685/month), vendor lock-in, complex local development with LocalStack, team would need to learn AWS-specific services |
| Redpanda/Kafka instead of AWS SNS/SQS | **Event Streaming**: Kafka supports event sourcing, CQRS, stream processing<br/>**Dapr Portability**: Can swap Kafka → RabbitMQ without code changes<br/>**Free Tier**: Redpanda Cloud serverless tier is free | **AWS SNS/SQS**: Limited to simple pub/sub, no stream processing, metered pricing, AWS lock-in |
| Dapr Distributed Runtime | **Infrastructure Abstraction**: Swap Redis → PostgreSQL state store without code changes<br/>**Polyglot Support**: Dapr supports multiple languages for future services<br/>**Sidecar Pattern**: Non-invasive observability and resilience | **Direct SDKs**: Tightly coupled to specific services (Redis, Kafka), language-specific, harder to swap infrastructure |

**Justification**: See [ADR 0001](../../history/adr/0001-kubernetes-over-serverless.md) for full rationale. Cost savings and portability outweigh operational complexity trade-offs.
